subject.title: PR1/6 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs

question: Should OpenClaw adopt, narrow, or reject the proposed owner-first residual durable-runtime boundary before this RFC is merged into the documentation source?
rationale: The patch deliberately avoids implementing behavior, but its central value is an architecture and ownership decision that source inspection and automated checks cannot make on behalf of maintainers.

options.title: Narrow and sponsor the RFC
options.body: Approve only the residual facts that do not duplicate existing TaskFlow, task, session, delivery, or subagent owners, then merge a correspondingly scoped proposal.

options.title: Adopt the proposed boundary
options.body: Accept the owner-first residual layer and enabled-only migration ownership as the basis for separately reviewed implementation work.

options.title: Reject shared residual state
options.body: Keep all remaining durable behavior inside existing owner-specific APIs and close this RFC without merging it.

recommendation.title: Narrow and sponsor the RFC
recommendation.body: Approve only the residual facts that do not duplicate existing TaskFlow, task, session, delivery, or subagent owners, then merge a correspondingly scoped proposal.

likelyOwner.reason: The merged TaskFlow substrate is the closest evidenced current owner boundary implicated by this RFC.
